Company Profile
Maruti Suzuki India Limited was established in 1981. A joint venture agreement was signed between the Government of India and 
Suzuki Motor Corporation (SMC), Japan in 1982. The Company became a subsidiary of SMC in 2002. In terms of production volume 
and sales, the Company is now SMC's largest subsidiary. As of 31st March 2026, SMC holds 58.53% of its equity stake. It is a public 
limited Company, and its shares are traded on the National Stock Exchange (NSE) and the Bombay Stock Exchange (BSE). The 
Company is the market leader of Passenger Vehicles (PVs) in India and is also the country’s largest exporter of PVs. In FY 2025-26, 
the Company posted its highest-ever total sales, surpassing the milestone of 2 million units for the third year in a row. The Company 
is the first among PV manufacturers in India to achieve this milestone.

Message from the Chairman
It gives me immense pleasure to welcome all of you to this the 45th annual general meeting of Maruti Suzuki India Limited. As we have 
been doing in the past, and in accordance with the existing law and rules on the subject, the meeting is being held virtually. One clear 
benefit of this system is that it enables shareholders to participate, and ask questions, from any part of the world. Physical meetings 
would not enable this to happen unless outstation shareholders incurred substantial costs to travel and stay at the meeting place.
In the last AGM I expressed my optimism about the future of the car industry, and especially of small cars, after the Prime Minister’s 
announcement that the GST system would be reformed from September 22nd. This happened and I am happy to inform you that these 
reforms have given a new impetus not only to the automobile industry but to several sectors of the economy. National GDP growth 
figures since then have been better than were forecast by most agencies. Despite the Iran-US war, that has adversely affected most 
global economies, the Indian economy continues to do well and remains the fastest growing among larger countries. GST collections, 
despite rates of tax being reduced on over 90% of products, have shown buoyancy and reached new high levels. I believe that without 
GST reforms we may not have done so well in the difficult months that have elapsed. On behalf of all of you I would like to convey our 
humble congratulations to the Prime Minister, the finance minister and all other members of the government. 
I would urge the government, including the State governments, to proceed faster on the road of reforms. Increase efforts to make 
doing business easier. Use more technology as it has shown that it reduces corruption and delays. Time saving is a major factor in 
lowering costs of production. Trust the private sector and the power of competition. Faster creation of wealth, in the most efficient 
manner, is the only way that India can make up for the time that we have lost. This has been demonstrated by the automobile sector. 
Large employment opportunities have opened up in the economy due to the growth of a competitive automobile industry. My request 
to all political parties is to support reforms and programmes that create wealth. The government, and the opposition, should ensure 
that the additional resources that would be generated would be used to create a more equitable and just society.
The financial year 2025-26 was a record year for your company. We achieved the highest level of sales of 24.22 lakh vehicles, highest 
exports of 4.47 lakh cars, highest production of 23.4 lakh cars and highest consolidated revenues of ` 1.83 lakh crores. The Annual 
profit at INR 14,445.4 crores was the highest ever. Our share price rose to ` 17,370 in January 2026 before the war brought down the 
entire market. As a result, your Board has been able to recommend a dividend of ` 140 on a share with face value of ` 5, the highest 
ever. This is consistent with the dividend policy and takes into account the massive investments being made by your company. I do 
hope you will support this recommendation. 
Overall, after the implementation of the new GST rates on the 22nd of September 2025, MSIL retail sales grew 17% in the second half 
of last year. We ended March with 1.9 lakh pending bookings, a result of inadequate manufacturing capacity of the models in demand. 
This was the consequence of adjustments made over the past several years to cater to the fall in small car sales and the growth of 
the SUV market. We are remedying this situation by making all our new production lines flexible enough to permit your company to 
change platforms and models as may be required. This is already showing results. In the first quarter of this year your company’s sales 
grew by 38%, while industry grew 28%. The sales of small cars grew 17% in the second half of last year but grew 35% in quarter 1 
this year as more cars required by customers could be produced. Your company is in the process of making as accurate an estimate 
as possible of the likely growth of the car market in the next five years, a happy exercise necessitated by the GST reforms. This could 
lead to some changes in our longer-term targets. Presently, we are estimating that the car industry would grow to 6.1 to 6.3 million by 
FY 2030-31 and that the share of the small car market would grow significantly faster than what had happened in the last five years. 
Your company has introduced an electric SUV, and it has been well received. 40,873 units of the EV have been exported so far and 
domestic sales during the first quarter were at 5,648. We have been comfortably meeting all the regulatory requirements and expect 
to continue to do so in the future.

Your company now has almost a 50% share of the cars exported from India. Japan has become our third largest export market. 
Export volumes are targeted to increase from last year’s level, despite the problems in the middle east.
Two lines have been commissioned in Kharkhoda and work is progressing on the third line. A fourth line of 250,000 capacity was 
commissioned at Hansalpur, raising installed capacity to 1 million. This is Suzuki’s largest plant anywhere in the world. Work has 
started at a new site in Sanand in Gujarat, and it is intended to install a total capacity of 1 million units there. The proposed investment 
at the Sanand site is ` 35,000 crores. As a result of the expansion projects, our installed capacity would reach 2.9 million units at the 
end of FY 2026-27 and 3.65 million units at the end of FY 2030-31. 
Our economy has a huge potential for growth. The government is committed to taking the economy along a sustained high growth 
path. The automotive industry will follow as the ability to commute comfortably and safely is a constituent of a developed economy. 
Your company is planning ahead on how to continue to play a leadership role in the future. We have to take into account not only 
the implications of artificial intelligence but also, as good citizens, to ensure that we play our part in meeting all the requirements of 
environmental protection and safety.
